title: Remote MCP hardening + cross-surface parity (supersedes the packet's Phase 2 proposal)

idea.problem: The Codex packet's 12-remote-mcp-proposal.yaml asks for a remote Streamable HTTP endpoint that already exists (omnarai.vercel.app/api/mcp, live and registered since 2026-07-16). What remains is not transport work but posture and parity: the endpoint's public read-only policy is de facto rather than documented, and tool definitions now exist in three places (stdio TOOLS, openai-tools.json, engine _mcp.js) with api/_inquiry.js as a manual keep-in-sync copy of inquiry.js.
idea.proposed_direction: Replace the packet's Phase 2 with a bounded hardening pass: document the public read-only access policy (Origin/auth/rate-limit stance made explicit), define a cross-repo tool-definition parity policy (automated check or documented duplication), and assert that Decision Ledger tools never appear on the remote surface.
idea.intended_outcome: The remote endpoint's trust boundary is stated rather than implied, drift between the three tool surfaces is detectable, and mutation authority provably stays out of the remote lane.

uncertainties: Whether cross-repo parity should be automated (shared module or CI check spanning omnarai-mcp and omnarai-memory-engine) or remain a documented manual release-checklist item.
Whether any rate limiting should be added at the endpoint or left to platform-level protections, given Hobby-plan constraints.

dissent.claim: A public unauthenticated endpoint invites abuse and cost.
dissent.response: The surface is read-oriented and the expensive council path is the same one already exposed via public HTTP APIs; the proposal documents this stance instead of pretending the endpoint is private.

proposal.decision: Do NOT build the packet's Phase 2. Instead: (1) publish a written access policy for /api/mcp (public read-only, CORS stance, what is and is not rate limited); (2) adopt a cross-surface parity policy covering stdio TOOLS, openai-tools.json, and engine _mcp.js, plus the _inquiry.js copy; (3) add an explicit assertion/test that no decision-ledger or other write tool ships on the remote surface.
scope: Access-policy documentation for the remote endpoint (engine repo).
Cross-surface parity policy and, if chosen, an automated check.
Remote-surface exclusion assertion for decision tools.
non_goals: Authentication/OAuth work, new transports, or session state.
Remote approval, contribution writes, publishing, or deployment tools.
acceptance_criteria: A visiting agent can read the endpoint's access policy and trust boundary.
A tool-definition change in one surface is caught (by check or checklist) before release.
The remote tools/list provably never includes the decision-ledger tools.
verification_plan: Live curl of /api/mcp tools/list (with x-omnarai-self header) compared against the stdio surface.
Parity check run across both repositories.
Review of the published access-policy text.

approval.note: Approved via Claude Code chat ("approve proposed"). Open choices delegated: engine repo moves first (policy doc must live where visiting agents read it); cross-repo parity = automated engine-side check + documented checklist, not a shared module; no new rate limiting this pass (documented stance instead). Chat approval is an attestation recorded here, not a verified identity.
